title: Rolling 30-Day Distinct Customer Count
description: For each order date in the table, count the number of **distinct customers who placed at least one order in the 30 days up to and including that date**. This simulates a rolling 30-day active user metric.
solution_sql: SELECT o1.order_date, COUNT(DISTINCT o2.customer_id) AS rolling_30d_customers FROM (SELECT DISTINCT order_date FROM orders) o1 JOIN orders o2 ON o2.order_date BETWEEN o1.order_date - INTERVAL '29 days' AND o1.order_date GROUP BY o1.order_date ORDER BY o1.order_date

test_cases.description: 12 distinct order dates, each showing distinct customers active in the prior 30 days up to that date

hints: Self-join orders: for each distinct order_date (o1), join all orders (o2) where o2.order_date falls within a 29-day lookback window ending on o1.order_date.
Use COUNT(DISTINCT o2.customer_id) to count unique customers in the window — a customer ordering twice in the window is counted once.
explanation: The self-join approach computes rolling windows without requiring window function DISTINCT support. For each unique date in o1, o2 joins all orders within the [date-29 days, date] range. COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) counts unique customers in that window. Jan 1: only C1 = 1. Jan 25: C1(Jan1,Jan15)+C2(Jan5,Jan25)+C3(Jan10)+C4(Jan20) = 4. This rolling metric is the foundation of Monthly Active Users (MAU) calculations.
